notes: The diagram labels prefetch_buffer_inst and neorv32_cpu_decompressor_inst as another-IP black boxes, so their data behavior is assessed using the specified black-box assumption.
Several conceptual assets enter or leave through fields of bus request or response records; those fields are included as structural assets but are barred from primary status by the Phase 2 rules.

points.reason: The response data directly changes the buffered instruction words through ipb.wdata, but this internal write-data path does not itself expose or block the instruction stream.
By the black-box FIFO assumption, response data entering the instance is stored and returned through ipb.rdata, while clear, write and read controls can discard or withhold instruction words.
This generate branch returns buffered instruction data and valid status directly, so the branch can expose or alter the instruction stream and can withhold it through ipb.avail.
The alignment-selected ipb.rdata word becomes issue.cmd16 and the issue acknowledgements control buffer reads, allowing selection or withholding of the instruction.
By the black-box rule, issue.cmd16 is transformed into issue.cmd32, which is the instruction value subsequently used by this unit.
This process selects compressed or full-width instruction data, drives the instruction and format outputs, and gates valid issue on buffer availability.
The registered alignment state changes which buffered word and instruction format the issue process selects, and therefore can steer or delay instruction delivery.
The response error bit is written into the buffered word, so it can be forged or suppressed and can cause the later fault indication to be wrong.
By the black-box FIFO assumption, the error bit is buffered with the instruction and can be discarded or withheld by the buffer controls.
The disabled branch reports the buffered error bit as frontend_o.fault, so the reported status can be forged and can signal a fault instead of allowing the required instruction transfer.
This process selects the buffered error bit for frontend_o.fault, allowing the status to be changed or used to indicate a failed fetch.

points.reached by: the prefetch_buffer_inst --> frontend_o and prefetch_buffer_inst --> fetch_fsm arrows
points.reason: The FIFO produces the availability and free-space indicators, and its clear, write and read controls can make valid data unavailable or report incorrect buffer space.
fetch.state controls the halted output condition and request sequencing, so an incorrect state can falsely halt or permit transfer.
The alignment state selects the issue branch and therefore controls which availability conditions drive valid output.
The process computes frontend_o.valid from buffer availability and alignment, so it can report a false status or withhold acceptance.
The disabled branch directly uses ipb.avail(0) as frontend_o.valid, allowing the availability status to be altered or suppressed.
The concurrent halted assignment makes buffer space and fetch state visible as a status that can block continued operation.
The process stores and advances fetch.pc, and the stored value is emitted as the instruction-bus address; changing it redirects or can prevent required fetches.
The concurrent address assignment exposes fetch.pc and lets an incorrect address steer the external instruction fetch.
The process stores the privilege mode and later copies the input mode into fetch.priv, so a changed mode can alter the protection context or cause a fetch to be rejected.
The request privilege field is driven directly from fetch.priv, so the emitted access context can be changed and can affect whether the fetch succeeds.
The debug attribute is copied directly to the bus request, so an attacker able to alter ctrl_i.cpu_debug can forge or suppress the fetch context.
The fence attribute is copied directly to the instruction-bus request, so changing ctrl_i.if_fence changes the ordering requirement observed by the bus.
The fetch process stores, retains and clears fetch.restart, so changing the input or its state updates can spuriously restart the sequence or prevent normal progress.
The retained restart value drives the FIFO clear input; by the black-box FIFO rule, repeated assertion can discard prefetched instructions and prevent continued operation.
fetch.restart controls the alignment-state update, so restart handling can alter the subsequent issue path and delay or disrupt normal instruction delivery.
